message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value (Standard Conditions) | Notes |
|----------|-----------------------------|-------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 | Only one proton in the nucleus. |
| **Symbol** | H | |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average) | Weighted average of isotopes; most common isotope is protium (^1H). |
| **Isotopes** | ^1H (protium), ^2H (deuterium), ^3H (tritium) | Deuterium and tritium are stable/long‑lived; tritium is radioactive. |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ | |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 | Highest among all elements. |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV | Highest of all elements. |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV | Negative value indicates energy release when an electron is added. |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) | Extremely low; hydrogen is a gas at room temperature. |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) | |
| **Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm)** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ | Very light; less dense than air. |
| **Molar volume (ideal gas)** | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ | |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; forms hydrides with metals, acids, and many nonmetals. | Forms H₂O, H₂S, HF, etc. |
| **Bonding** | Covalent (H–H single bond), ionic (as H⁺ or H⁻), metallic (in some alloys). | |
| **Acidity/basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming H₃O⁺) and a weak base (forming H₂O). | |
| **Oxidation states** | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (molecular H₂). | |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman, Balmer series in UV/visible; prominent in stellar spectra. | |
| **Physical state** | Gas at STP; liquid under high pressure; solid at very low temperatures. | |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant, industrial hydrogenation, metallurgy, semiconductor manufacturing. | |

### Quick Summary

- **Lightest element**: only one proton and one electron.
- **Highly electronegative**: strongest attraction for electrons among all elements.
- **High ionization energy**: difficult to remove its lone electron.
- **Very low boiling/melting points**: remains gaseous under normal conditions.
- **Versatile chemistry**: forms hydrides, acids, bases, and covalent bonds with many elements.
- **Key isotopes**: protium (^1H), deuterium (^2H), tritium (^3H); the latter two are used in nuclear fusion research and radiolabeling.

These properties make hydrogen unique and essential in both natural processes (e.g., photosynthesis, combustion) and advanced technologies (fuel cells, fusion reactors).
